title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: Context (cote 140-4, the continuation of 'La Longue Marche'): Grothendieck is building group schemes over a base S_0 that model the automorphism groups relevant to the Teichmüller group M_{1,1} (the next page writes M = N_{1,1}^{ét}). They are meant to receive canonical homomorphisms from M, 'relative to the tower of Fermat curves', after taking Ẑ-points (next page, (216)-(217)). The notation is as follows. M~_{ρ,σ} is a semidirect product Φ_12^*·(G × S^+). Its elements are written (λ,x).μ with μ = (ν_2, ν_3, ν_0) in a character-type group Φ_12^2. The indices 2, 3, 0 plausibly refer to the elliptic points of orders 2 and 3 and to the cusp; 12 = |SL_2(Z)^ab|. The previous page defined the subgroup M~_{ρ,σ}(-j̄) as the set of (λ,x).μ such that x·u_μ ∈ N_ρ, where u_μ is the canonical element from (151). It then showed that v = σ^{ν_3} δ^{-ν''} u_μ, with δ = λ_1 λ_0^{-1}, lies in Γ N_ρ ∩ G_{ρ,σ} = Γ Z_ρ. This page finishes that computation. (i) For each μ ∈ Γ Φ_12^2, the fibre of N_ρ^! over μ is the set (212) {ω^i σ^{-ν_3} δ^{-ν''} u_μ | i ∈ Γ{0,1}_{S_0}}. So it is a two-element torsor, twisted by an order-two element ω. Because i is a section of the constant scheme {0,1}, the choice of ω^0 or ω^1 may vary over the connected components of S_0. (ii) Hence (213): M~_{ρ,σ}(-j) consists of the (λ,x).μ with x = ω^i σ^{-ν_3} δ^{-ν''} u_μ. (iii) Intersecting with the 'bilateral' subgroup M^{⇄}_{ρ,σ} kills both the ω-ambiguity and the ν_3-component. This gives (214): M'~_{ρ,σ}(-j) = {(λ, δ^{-ν''}).μ | μ ∈ Γ Φ_12^{*1}, i.e. ε_3(μ) = 0, λ ∈ Γ G_m (or G_a), ν'' = ν''(μ)}. The page then breaks off at a dangling '='. The purpose is to describe explicitly the stabilizer-type subgroups inside the semidirect product. On the next page their Ẑ-points become Ẑ^*-semidirect products, which are targets of the outer Galois/Teichmüller action on the Fermat tower.
errors: Sign inconsistency in the exponent of σ. The previous page writes v = σ^{ν_3} δ^{-ν''} u_μ, while this page's (212)/(213) use σ^{-ν_3} (σ is visibly overwritten in the image). One of the two is a slip, or a convention change in mid-computation.
The equation number (212) is used twice: once on the previous page for v = τ'^{ν_3}(...) and again here for (N_ρ^!)_μ.
The factor under λ is written G_a on the previous page and in (213), but G_m in (214); the notation is unstable.
Gap: (214) asserts without argument that the intersection with M^{⇄} forces i = 0 and ε_3(μ) = 0. The final '=' is left unfinished.

ideas.what: Explicit description of a stabilizer-type subgroup of a semidirect product group scheme Φ_12^*·(G × S^+), via a fibre that is a 2-element torsor indexed by locally constant sections i ∈ Γ{0,1}_{S_0}
ideas.modern_name: computation of normalizers/centralizers in a semidirect product group scheme; twisted forms over a non-connected base
ideas.where_published: Not in the published 'Longue Marche' text as far as known; part of its unpublished continuation

ideas.what: Group schemes over Z (Ẑ-points with componentwise sections, '^Δ') as targets of homomorphisms from the étale Teichmüller group M_{1,1}, relative to the Fermat curve tower
ideas.modern_name: metabelian / Fermat-tower quotient of the outer Galois action on π_1(P^1 − {0,1,∞}); Anderson–Ihara-type 'Jacobi sum' descriptions
ideas.where_published: Theme sketched in Esquisse d'un programme; this specific formalism is unpublished

missed.claim: The explicit computation of the subgroups M~_{ρ,σ}(-j) and M'~_{ρ,σ}(-j) is part of an unpublished, group-scheme-theoretic formalism for the M_{1,1}/Fermat-tower metabelian action. It stops mid-equation. Its relation to Ihara's and Anderson's Fermat-tower Galois representations has not been worked out in the literature.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could provide an arithmetic-group-scheme packaging of the metabelian Galois/Teichmüller action including M_{1,1}. This page alone is a routine step, however.

deep.surprise_reason: A technical intermediate computation inside an unpublished formalism. The overall programme (Galois/Teichmüller action through the Fermat tower) is notable but known in spirit (Ihara, Anderson), and this page adds only a routine subgroup description.
transcription_corrections: In (212) the σ factor is σ^{-ν_3}; an earlier glyph is overwritten by σ.
The first line likely reads 'Or on voit que v ∈ N_ρ^?' with a crossed-out symbol before N_ρ.
In (213) the group under λ appears as G_a (consistent with the previous page) rather than G_m; in (214) it reads Γ G_m.
The index set is written 'i ∈ Γ{0,1}_{S_0}' (sections of the constant scheme {0,1} over S_0).
In (214) the superscript of M is M^{⇄} (double arrow) and μ ∈ Γ Φ_12^{*1}.
